subject: general
question: If LCM (27, n) = 54 and HCF (27, n) = 9, then the value of n is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **product of two numbers** is always equal to the product of their **LCM** and **HCF**.

First number × Second number = **LCM** × **HCF**

27 × **n** = 54 × 9

**n** = (54 × 9) ÷ 27 = 2 × 9 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First number = 27, **LCM(27, n)** = 54, **HCF(27, n)** = 9.

**Formula Used:** Product of two numbers = **LCM** × **HCF**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a88457e648797926f49308946ca30386f44d8b873033fb96431daab4c65d56f6.png] 

⇒ 27 × n = 54 × 9

⇒ 27n = 486

⇒ n = 486 ÷ 27

⇒ n = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Property of LCM and HCF

For any two positive integers a and b, the relationship is defined as: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

Divisibility Rule

The **HCF** of any group of numbers is always a factor of their **LCM**. Here, 9 is a factor of 54.

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are **co-prime**, their **HCF** is 1, and their **LCM** is the product of the numbers themselves.</p
